Article Title: Mizoram's 'misogynistic' marriage, divorce law faces challenge in SC
Article Text:
Mizo woman challenges marriage law in SC, calls it ‘misogynistic and pro-Mizo men’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Entrepreneur and Congress functionary Meriam L Hrangchal Monday challenged the constitutional validity of Mizo Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance of Property Act, 2014, which was enacted by Congress govt headed by Lal Thanhawla, terming it "misogynistic and pro-Mizo men".Hrangchal, daughter of former deputy CM Lalhmingthanga, told a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant that the law, which codified customary law, applied to any person belonging to a Mizo tribe and extended to marriages where the male member belonged to a Mizo tribe.The 2014 Act denies Mizo women, who marry outside the Mizo community, access to a comprehensive community-specific statutory framework governing marriage, property and inheritance, thereby infringing their right to equality, dignity and personal liberty under Articles 14 and 21, she said.The law marginalises the independent identity of Mizo women and refuses them the benefits under the 2014 Act which extends to marriage between a Mizo man and a non-Mizo woman but does not cover marriage between a Mizo woman and a non-Mizo man, she said, citing her own marital relationship."The effect of such provisions is that Mizo women who marry non-Mizo men, and the children born out of such marriages, are excluded from the statutory regime, notwithstanding their subsisting connection to the Mizo community," she said.The bench said the issue raised in her petition was important but asked why she was bypassing the high court. Her counsel said the community being small, she feared for her safety if her petition was heard by the Aizawl bench of Gauhati HC.The CJI-led bench understood her apprehension and requested the CJ of Gauhati HC to hear her petition in Guwahati without sending it to the Aizawl bench.
Article Summary: Mizo woman challenges marriage law in SC, calls it ‘misogynistic and pro-Mizo men’ Meriam L Hrangchal challenges the constitutional validity of Mizo Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance of Property Act, 2014.

CM Yogi targets Congress state

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday stepped up his attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the Manusmriti, while also targeting the party's state leadership over its alleged conduct in Ayodhya.Speaking in Raebareli, CM Yogi said Rahul Gandhi, as leader of opposition, had a responsibility to uphold the Constitution and respect India's traditions and heritage.“Recently, I was reading a statement made by the Member of Parliament from Raebareli, Rahul Gandhi. He made a statement in Maharashtra urging women to break free from the shackles of the Manusmriti. Rahul ji, the country does not have high expectations of you merely as Rahul Gandhi; in fact, it has no expectations at all. However, your role as the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament entails accountability towards the country's democracy. You took an oath to uphold the Constitution of India, yet you seem to consider it your birthright to disparage India's traditions and heritage.”CM Yogi accused Gandhi of insulting Uttar Pradesh and India during visits outside the state and abroad. He also alleged that the Congress had questioned the existence of Lord Ram in Ayodhya and referred to the Emergency imposed in 1975.The UP chief minister said Rahul Gandhi should study ancient Indian texts to understand Manu and India's heritage.“You make comments regarding Manu, Ram, or India's heritage. If you wish to understand Manu, read the Atharvaveda, the Shatapatha Brahmana and the Matsya Purana; you will find all the information there.”Yogi also criticised remarks directed at the Prime Minister, saying such statements amounted to an attack on an institution rather than an individual.“When you insult India's institutions, when you make derogatory remarks about the Prime Minister of India, you are not merely insulting an individual; you are insulting an institution of India. The Prime Minister is not just an individual; the Prime Minister is an institution of India.”He added that such criticism could undermine public confidence in constitutional institutions and urged Gandhi to refrain from what he called irresponsible behaviour.CM Yogi also attacked the Congress state president over an alleged incident involving a visit to Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya, accusing him of displaying duplicity.“You saw the behaviour of the Congress state president: he goes to offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, but later outside he enjoys a feast of fish. He could have eaten whatever he wanted outside—anywhere other than Ayodhya. Yet, this is the duplicity they display. Even a chameleon would be put to shame by these people; it would wonder what kind of human species this is—chanting 'Ram-Ram' inside the temple and feasting on fish the moment they step out. This is their history—the history of this Congress state president.”CM Yogi further alleged that the Congress leader had bowed before a mafia figure who had allegedly killed his brother, claiming the situation changed only after the government acted against the accused.“When a mafia don murdered his brother, this man did not testify against the criminal; instead, he knelt and bowed in submission before him. He knelt before the very man who had brutally killed his brother. It was only when the government stepped in and crushed that mafia element that the situation changed; otherwise, these people had turned the state into a mafia-dominated territory, creating an identity crisis.”CM Yogi also said society could have no future if it forgot its ancestors and accused unnamed groups of attempting to weaken India's traditions, values and ideals.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath steps up his attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on the Manusmriti. He also targets the party's state leadership over its alleged conduct in Ayodhya. CM Yogi said Rahul Gandhi had a responsibility to uphold the Constitution and respect India's traditions and heritage.

The Federation of Seafarers and Indian Seafarers Union (FSUI) has released an old video showing a vessel carrying 22 crew members, including 21 Indians, coming under attack in the Strait of Hormuz on April 22.The footage shows several small boats surrounding the vessel, an RPG being fired and seafarers rushing to the ship’s alleyways to take cover as the confrontation unfolded.The union also released images showing crew members taking cover while the vessel was under attack.“These were not pirates. They were naval forces of the IRGC,” the FSUI said in a post on X.The union added that the footage highlighted the risks faced by seafarers in the Strait of Hormuz, arguing that advisories and guidelines alone could not ensure their safety.“Innocent seafarers need the assured presence of naval forces to truly protect them,” the FSUI said.The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) recently said 166 Indian seafarers remained in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz region, including 125 aboard six Indian-flagged vessels and 41 working on foreign-flagged ships.In an update on August 4, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways said 3,972 Indian seafarers had been repatriated from the Gulf region, highlighting the scale of the effort to bring them out of the conflict zone.India is the world’s second-largest supplier of seafarers after the Philippines, with 311,936 personnel accounting for 12.16 per cent of the global maritime workforce, according to the BIMCO-ICS Seafarer Workforce Report 2026. Indian officers account for 13.41 per cent of the global officer workforce, while 171,218 Indian ratings make up 11.29 per cent of the global ratings workforce.The large presence of Indian seafarers in the region has also resulted in casualties since the Iran war began. Last month, the MEA said Indian seafarers had recorded the highest number of fatalities among all nationalities in attacks on commercial shipping.The government later informed Parliament that 10 Indian seafarers were among the 16 Indian nationals killed in the Middle East conflict.
Article Summary: The Federation of Seafarers and Indian Seafarers Union (FSUI) has released an old video showing a vessel carrying 22 crew members, including 21 Indians, coming under attack. The footage shows several small boats surrounding the vessel, an RPG being fired and seafarers rushing to the ship’s alleyways to take cover as the confrontation unfolded.

Article Title: Repeated trips of Turkish military transport planes to Pak between Aug 19 & 21 raise eyebrows in India
Article Text:
Spike in Turkish military flights to Pakistan raises concerns over possible weapons transfers

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan in the last few days has raised hackles in Indian defence circles.Open-source flight trackers noted a 60-hour surge of Turkish military transport flights, including Turkish C-130 Hercules and A400M aircraft (such as one with call sign TUAF526), landing at Pakistani air bases like Nur Khan, Masroor, and Murid between August 19 and 21.There is speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried Turkish military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems (drones) and air-defence equipment like Baykar (next-generation kamikaze UAV K2) and Asisguard systems (drone systems) to Pakistan. The aircraft movements were seen soon after after the signing of the tripartite Mecca Joint Defence Agreement between Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia on Aug 7. The agreement establishes a collective defence pact, stating that an armed attack against any one of the three member states will be considered an attack against all of them.However, neither Pakistan nor Turkey has officially confirmed the precise nature or cargo of these transport operations.With Turkish aircraft landing in Pakistan, questions are being raised in defence circles whether Pakistan is gearing up for another conflict with India.Before Operation Sindoor in May last year, China and Turkey had allegedly supplied Pakistan with advanced military hardware, including Chinese PL-15 air-to-air missiles and HQ-9 air defence systems, and Turkish-origin Bayraktar (Yiha) and Asisguard Songar kamikaze drones. They also provided real-time battlefield data and tactical support.During the four-day conflict last year, the Indian armed forces tackled these attacks using their multilayered air defence grid and integrated command and control strategy, successfully intercepting all incoming aerial threats before reaching critical military or civilian infrastructure.The Indian forces deployed indigenous technology and advanced anti-access frameworks to crush the Pakistan defence network and also thwarted its offensive attacks. The IAF used long-range capabilities of Russian-acquired S-400 Triumf air defence system and indigenous Akash-NG missiles to thwart missile and UAV attacks. The IAF also used the S-400 to shoot down a high-value Pakistani Saab 2000 Erieye AEW&C surveillance aircraft from around 314 km away — which stands as one of the longest-range combat surface-to-air missile engagements in military history.
Article Summary: An unusual increase in Turkish military transport flights to Pakistan in the last few days has raised hackles in Indian defence circles. Speculation in defence circles that the flights may have carried Turkish military hardware, including unmanned aerial systems (drones) and air-defence equipment.

Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi's new playbook shows a more persistent style, combining youth outreach, and surprise street protests.

Has Rahul evolved as a leader?

NEW DELHI:There is a visible change in how Rahul Gandhi pushes through issues now. The leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha has a new weapon in his political arsenal: impromptu protests.For the second time in a month, the Congress leader caught the authorities and, to some extent, even his own party, off guard by taking to the streets of the national capital without prior warning.When Rahul reached the DCP office in Delhi on August 21 demanding an FIR for Sahil Lochab, who sustained pellet injuries during the July 20 student protest, it was Act 2 of his new playbook of street protest politics.When the cops dilly-dallied, Rahul refused to budge and staged a sit-in protest outside the police station. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined him. Congress leaders began arriving. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed outside.A visit to a police office turned into a high-voltage political stand-off and, after six hours of dharna, Delhi Police registered an FIR over the pellet firing.The BJP reacted sharply, calling Rahul's sit-in the 'politics of anarchy'. It argued that an FIR relating to the wider July 20 incident already existed, an investigation was under way and the Congress leader was turning police procedure into a political spectacle.For Lochab, however, there was a sense of relief. His family had been trying to get his complaint registered since August 14, shuttling between police stations. The 19-year-old, who underwent surgery after pellets struck his right eye, finally had an FIR registered after Rahul’s intervention.For years, opponents have labelled Rahul Gandhi a 'part-time politician' who would raise an issue and then disappear. But this incident reinforced something that has changed about Rahul’s tactics over the past year. He is no longer content merely to raise an issue. He increasingly wants to enter it, stay with it and, if necessary, physically occupy the space.The first display of this surprise street-politics instinct had come a month earlier during the NEET student protests.On July 21, a day after police used force to stop thousands of students attempting a 'Sansad Chalo' march over exam irregularities, Rahul suddenly headed towards Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence and staged a sit-in.Police had reportedly made arrangements anticipating a Congress protest at Vijay Chowk. Rahul went to Lok Kalyan Marg instead. The move caught security officials by surprise. Rahul, Priyanka and several other opposition leaders were later detained. The visual that immediately took over the news was hard to ignore: the leader of opposition physically struggling with police officers, being dragged away and getting a nosebleed in the chaos.That was Act 1.It came at a time when the Congress was desperately trying to make its presence felt, with Abhijeet Dipke’s Cockroach Janata Party and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk already leading a massive student protest against the NEET paper leak.Congress had initially kept its distance, preferring to run its own youth outreach campaign, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj'. But people asked a simple question: If Congress claimed to support student issues, why was it missing from the biggest student movement in Delhi?When the July 20 Jantar Mantar protest took place and massive outrage erupted over police action against the student protesters, Rahul's approach changed.The very next day, he moved to the front lines. He stood outside the Prime Minister's house, Congress leaders visited injured students, and police action became a major national debate. Rahul took the issue to Parliament and continued raising the pitch over injuries suffered by students.And when the larger protest began to recede from the headlines, Rahul stayed with one part of it: the use of pellet guns. He has affirmed that his party will keep raising the issue and demand accountability.The first major image makeover was when Rahul Gandhi embarked on the ' Bharat Jodo Yatra ' from Kanyakumari to Kashmir in 2022. Sceptics and rivals wondered if he would complete the journey. By the time he reached Kashmir months later, after walking thousands of kilometres in his now-signature white T-shirt, one charge had become considerably harder to make: that Rahul was unwilling to put in the physical grind that it takes in politics.The yatra, on its own, did not help the Congress much. What it did was change the way Rahul himself was seen as a politician.For months, people saw him walking with the common public rather than delivering a scripted speech from a podium. He met farmers, labourers and students, stopped for conversations, entered homes and sat and ate with people.The yatra experience also laid the foundation for his growing social media popularity. His online presence today increasingly relies on short, conversational exchanges that can easily travel as reels and clips.The second shift came in 2024, when he became the leader of the opposition.Since then, we have seen a more combative Rahul Gandhi. Whether one agrees with his politics or the issues he raises, he appears considerably more comfortable with confrontation than he once did.Congress's protests in the Parliament complex have also become more visual and experimental under Rahul.He repeatedly joined opposition MPs at Makar Dwar over the Election Commission’s SIR exercise in Bihar, with MPs carrying 'vote chori' placards and demanding its rollback. The protest later moved beyond the Parliament gates, with Rahul and other opposition leaders marching towards the Election Commission before being stopped and detained.Rahul provokes ministers across the aisle and stays for the response. He takes an argument from the street into Parliament and, increasingly, carries it back outside again. This is also a part of his renewed Gen Z outreach.If Bharat Jodo helped Rahul Gandhi build the image of a politician who was more approachable and willing to listen, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' took that idea to a more specific audience: Gen Z.The programme began in Kota, where students spoke about paper leaks, recruitment delays, coaching pressure and the uncertainty around exams and jobs. The format was less rally and more conversation, with Rahul asking questions, listening, and allowing individual experiences to shape the message. That made the outreach more relatable.His latest Pune edition further widened that outreach by putting young women at the centre of the conversation.Rahul's call to 'smash the patriarchy' in a stadium full of women was a strong message that came with its own set of criticism. He spoke about different social expectations for boys and girls, cited the 'Manusmriti' while attacking the BJP-RSS worldview, and told women that they 'belong' to themselves rather than to fathers, husbands or sons, triggering huge applause from the crowd.While a large section of people lauded the focus on women, the ruling BJP immediately trained its guns on him and asked him to induct women ministers into the Karnataka cabinet, where Congress is in power.Even as Rahul attacked the BJP over issues such as NEET and paper leaks, major student protests broke out in Jharkhand, where the Congress shares power in the Hemant Soren government. Soon after the Jantar Mantar agitation ended, aspirants took to the streets in Ranchi over alleged irregularities and paper leaks in JPSC and JSSC examinations.This time, the criticism was closer to home. Protesters targeted not just chief minister Hemant Soren but Rahul as well, pointing to the irony of him speaking for students nationally while Congress was part of the ruling alliance in Jharkhand. Effigies of both leaders were burnt, and Rahul was accused of not speaking about Jharkhand issues.Eventually, Rahul was forced to react and intervene. He asserted that Congress supported students protesting peacefully and said that dialogue was the only way forward.Rahul wrote an open letter to Soren, requesting the CM to personally meet the students and hear out their grievances. The Jharkhand government later accepted the students' demands.The episode helped Rahul avoid the charge of being selective on student issues, but it also showed the challenge of claiming an issue as your own: once you do that, you can be questioned even when the government under fire is run by an ally.For years, Rahul Gandhi was accused of being an inconsistent politician who would raise important issues and then disappear from the conversation. Rivals branded him as an “entitled leader” and took “Pappu” digs at him.But the old image of Rahul as a reluctant politician is certainly harder to sustain today. From Bharat Jodo to 'Chhatron Ki Goonj', fiery parliamentary confrontations and surprise dharnas, he appears more comfortable playing on the front foot.However, his latest round of street protests seems to stem from the crisis that the opposition in general and Congress in particular faced as Abhijeet Dipke-led CJP mobilised youth in large numbers and forced the government to make Dharmendra Pradhan resign as Union education minister.Rahul has made his presence felt, but we will have to wait and see if his new politics translates into electoral success for the Congress.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi's new playbook shows a more persistent style, combining youth outreach, and surprise street protests. He is no longer content merely to raise an issue. He increasingly wants to enter it, stay with it and, if necessary, physically occupy it. For the second time in a month, the Congress leader caught the authorities off guard by taking to the streets of the national capital.

Article Title: SIA reopens probe into 1998 massacre of 23 Kashmiri Pandits in Ganderbal
Article Text:
SIA reopens 1998 Wandhama massacre probe, steps up investigation into Kashmiri Pandit killings

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: J&K State Investigation Agency (SIA) has reopened the investigation into the 1998 Wandhama massacre of 23 people as part of a wider push to probe the killings of Kashmiri Pandits during the peak of militancy in the Valley.According to sources, SIA has also started a probe into the killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandit advocate-politician Tika Lal Taploo and Justice Neelkanth Ganjoo.On Jan 25, 1998, armed terrorists entered the homes of Kashmiri Pandit families in Wandhama village of Ganderbal district and gunned down 23 people. The case still remains unresolved, but SIA sources in said it will see “substantial progress soon”.Officials said SIA has undertaken a focused and comprehensive investigation into the decades-old cases to bring each of these to a logical conclusion in accordance with law. “Concerted efforts are being made to uncover the circumstances and conspiracies underlying these cases, establish credible evidence, and identify those responsible strictly on the basis of substantiated evidence and witness testimony,” said an official.Taploo, a prominent lawyer and then vice-president of J&K BJP, was shot dead near his residence in Srinagar in Sept 1989, in what among the first targeted killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandits as terrorism took roots in the Valley.Justice Ganjoo, who had sentenced JKLF founder Maqbool Bhat to death, was shot dead on Nov 4, 1989 in Srinagar.On Aug 12, SIA carried out searches at nine locations across J&K in connection with the killing of Kashmiri Pandit poet and writer Sarvanand Kaul Premi and his son by terrorists. Premi, 66, and his younger son Verinder were shot dead in Anantnag in south Kashmir on May 1, 1990, a day after they were abducted from their village.Their bodies were later found hanging from a tree. Five days later, the grief-stricken Kaul family left Kashmir, never to return.Earlier on June 29, SIA filed a 737-page chargesheet in connection with the killing of Sarla Bhat, 27, a nurse at Srinagar’s Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences. She was abducted by terrorists from the SKIMS hostel on April 18, 1990, tortured and shot dead. Her bullet-riddled body was recovered the next day.
Article Summary: J&K State Investigation Agency (SIA) has reopened the investigation into the 1998 Wandhama massacre. SIA has also started a probe into the killings of prominent Kashmiri Pandit advocate-politician Tika Lal Taploo and Justice Neelkanth Ganjoo.

Article Title: 'Failure of judicial system': SC on 45-year-old case
Article Text:
SC frees bedridden convict as double murder case takes 44 years through courts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It took a lower court 22 years to complete trial in a double murder case and another 22 years for Jharkhand high court to decide the appeal, and during the long proceedings, five of six accused died and the sole surviving bed-ridden convict in his 70s is fighting a legal battle in Supreme Court from jail.Terming the inordinate delay in deciding the case a failure of the judicial system, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran suspended the sentence of the convict and allowed him to come out of jail on bail. It also decided to examine the reason why the trial court and HC took so long in deciding the case of double murder, which took place in 1981.The said case projects failure of the judicial system, when a crime went unpunished and the accused were put to the torture of a prolonged trial of 22 years and then after conviction, the appeal filed having been dismissed after yet another two decades and two years, SC said.Advocate Fauzia Shakil, appearing for the convict, submitted that the petitioner will suffer grave prejudice and irreparable loss if bail is not granted to him inasmuch as there cannot be any adequate compensation for his prolonged incarceration in the event of his eventual acquittal by SC.“Despite the horrendous crime of a double murder, we cannot close our eyes to the ordeal suffered by the accused in the last 45 years.Especially noting his medical condition and the affidavit of the state that the petitioner is admitted in the hospital, though in custody, we suspend the sentence and direct that the petitioner shall be released forthwith on condition of his not committing any crime when on bail and on his personal surety,” it said.“It is very disturbing to note that although the incident is of the year 1981 yet the judgement and order passed by the trial court holding the petitioner guilty of the alleged crime is of 2002. We fail to understand why it took 22 years for the trial court to complete the trial... Even HC took 22 years to decide the appeal preferred by the petitioner challenging the judgement and order of conviction passed by the trial court. This delay highlighted above is something very disturbing,” SC noted in its order.Asked by the court to give an explanation for the delay, the registrar general of HC told the court that the delay was also caused as the accused were absconding for six years. But the court noted that there is no explanation for the 12 years it took for the trial to be completed when the charges were framed in 1991.“We were concerned with pendency of the criminal appeals as pointed out in the report of HC and we hence thought it fit to permit the petitioner to implead Centre in the above matter. The learned advocate-on-record appearing for HC would serve a copy of the affidavit of compliance filed by the registrar general to the office of the attorney general/solicitor general,” the court said.
Article Summary: It took a lower court 22 years to complete trial in a double murder case. Another 22 years for Jharkhand high court to decide the appeal. During the long proceedings, five of six accused died. The sole surviving bed-ridden convict in his 70s is fighting a legal battle from jail.

Article Title: J&K CM Omar Abdullah asks police, security agencies to take poster threatening Kashmir Pandit employees seriously
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah flags fresh threats targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A new poster issued by the little-known United Liberation Council (ULC) threatening Kashmiri Pandits led community members working in the Kashmir Valley under the PM Package for Kashmiri Migrants and Non-Migrant Kashmiri Pandits to write to J&K chief secretary Atal Dulloo seeking enhanced security. Chief minister Omar Abdullah described the threats as “highly concerning.”The poster contains the personal details of some Kashmiri Pandit employees, including addresses.Omar, talking to reporters here, urged police and law-and-order agencies not to take the threats lightly. He said the agencies have a responsibility to provide security to Kashmiri Pandit employees and urged them to proactively investigate the source of the threats.“In a similar situation around two and a half years ago, some Pandit employees were targeted,” Omar said. He said security and law-and-order arrangements in J&K are under the control of the lieutenant-governor.The police have issued any statement on the fresh threat. The chief secretary was not available for comment.According to a letter from All PM Package Employees’ Forum to the CS, “a fresh threat poster, purportedly issued by a terrorist outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) on Aug 23, 2026, has surfaced on social media.The poster reportedly contains threats directed towards migrant Kashmiri Pandit employees and … details such as names, addresses and vehicle numbers of certain individuals.”While the forum said the “authenticity of the poster is yet to be verified by police and security agencies”, it added that “the repeated circulation of such threat letters and posters, particularly those containing sensitive personal information, is a matter of grave concern”.The forum sought a review of security arrangements at places of posting, residential accommodation and transit routes of PM Package employees. It said govt should ensure that employees whose names, addresses or vehicle details have appeared in such threats receive immediate protection and necessary security guidance.All Minority Employees Association president Sanjay Kaul said the Aug 23 poster was the third in 20 days. “We are only here for work. We take such threat letters seriously as they contain names and even numbers of vehicles of some Pandit employees,” Kaul said. “Before 2022 we were working fearlessly, but not now. We seek a thorough probe,” he added.In May 2022, Kashmiri Pandit migrant employee Rahul Bhat was shot dead by terrorists inside his office in central Kashmir’s Budgam district. He was recruited as a clerk under the PM Package for migrants in 2010-11.The Manmohan Singh-led UPA govt had in 2008 introduced a rehabilitation package for Kashmiri Pandits living outside the Valley, including providing 6,000 govt jobs and creation of new posts. Those recruited under the package are posted in various govt departments across Kashmir and commonly referred to as “PM package employees”.
Article Summary: A new poster issued by the little-known United Liberation Council (ULC) threatens Kashmiri Pandits. Chief minister Omar Abdullah described the threats as “highly concerning” The poster contains the personal details of some KashmiriPandit employees, including addresses.

Article Title: No alliance with SAD? BL Santosh says BJP to go solo in Punjab polls
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Monday put speculation over an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal to rest, saying the saffron party will contest all 117 seats in the upcoming Punjab assembly elections.BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh said the party was fully prepared for the polls and would form the government in Punjab."Punjab is fully ready for change, and the BJP is fully prepared to make this change a reality. In the upcoming assembly elections, the BJP will contest all 117 Assembly seats in Punjab and, by securing a victory, will form its government in the state," Santosh said.The statement comes days after speculation grew over a possible BJP-SAD alliance following SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal's meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Former Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal had also hinted at the possibility of the Akali Dal joining hands with the BJP again, while expressing a cryptic wish for "agreements" that brought progress to Punjab from Delhi.Earlier, Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia also said that people in Punjab want his party to join hands with the Bharatiya Janata Party for the upcoming polls.Majithia cited Punjab's status as a border state and the need to protect social harmony and the state's social fabric as reasons for public sentiment favouring a reunion."We should understand that the Shiromani Akali Dal and BJP have worked together. Vajpayee ji and Badal ji strengthened this alliance, and it continued during Modi ji's time," Majithia said.The SAD had parted ways with the National Democratic Alliance in September 2020 over the three farm laws, which were later repealed.Santosh began his two-day visit to Punjab to review the party's organisational functioning and strengthen coordination and preparedness at the grassroots level in the poll-bound state.His visit comes amid dissent within the BJP's state unit over a recent organisational reshuffle, with a section of leaders accusing the state leadership of sidelining the old cadre.
Article Summary: BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh said the party was fully prepared for the polls and would form the government in Punjab. Earlier, Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia also said that people in Punjab want his party to join hands with the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Article Title: 'Hindu baiter': CM Himanta slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti row
Article Text:
Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti comment. Photo credit: ANI

NEW DELHI: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Monday joined the escalating political row over Rahul Gandhi ’s remarks on the Manusmriti, accusing the Congress leader of using women’s rights as a 'smokescreen' to target Hinduism and challenging him to support a Uniform Civil Code (UCC).Sarma, in a post on X, said, “Rahul Gandhi is NO champion of women’s rights. He is simply a Hindu baiter, using the cause of women’s empowerment as a convenient smokescreen to target and discredit Hindu Dharma.”The Assam chief minister’s remarks came after Gandhi, during an interaction with girl students in Pune on Saturday, criticised what he called a “Manusmriti mindset” and urged women to “smash patriarchy”.Sarma questioned Gandhi’s position by asking, “Consider this: how many times has he spoken with the same outrage against patriarchal and medieval practices that persist under Sharia? NEVER.”He further argued that Manusmriti and Sharia should not be treated as equivalent sources of authority, writing, “While Sharia is foundational to Islamic jurisprudence, Manusmriti has no comparable scriptural authority in Hindu Dharma. It is not even a universally binding code for Hindus.”Sarma then directly challenged the Congress leader over the issue of a common civil law. “So here is a simple challenge to Rahul Gandhi: If women’s equality truly comes before politics, will he unequivocally support a Uniform Civil Code that guarantees equal rights irrespective of religion?” he said.Sarma also alleged that Congress had a record of compromising on women’s rights, referring to the Shah Bano case and the Triple Talaq legislation. He further claimed that Gandhi had ensured that no woman was included in the Karnataka state Cabinet.The remarks came after the LoP’s interaction with students, where he said women should not be defined solely through their relationships with men.Rahul said women belong to themselves and not to their fathers, husbands or sons, while describing as shameful the Manusmriti’s prescription that women remain under the authority of male relatives at different stages of their lives.Referring to a verse from the ancient text, Gandhi said, “These words are a shame. These words should not have been spoken.”The controversy has since widened, with Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis among other prominent BJP faces criticised Rahul’s remarks.CM Adityanath earlier questioned Gandhi’s role as Leader of Opposition and said, “Whether you accept the Manusmriti or not is your choice, but do not acquaint people with wrong facts.”
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma slams Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti comment. Accuses Congress leader of using women’s rights as a'smokescreen' to target Hinduism. Sarma also challenges Gandhi to support a Uniform Civil Code.

NEW DELHI: Abhijeet Dipke, founder and convenor of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), has demanded transparency on government school funding, infrastructure and staffing. Addressing an open letter to the education ministers across states, he said citizens have a right to know what steps are being taken to improve public education.He posed six questions to the ministers regarding the condition and facilities inside the government schools. He also asked them to publicly disclose details on infrastructure, teacher vacancies, funding, digital facilities and the workload of teaching staff.Dipke posted a letter on his X account with the caption, "Letter to the Education Ministers of all states. The country needs to know what steps are being taken to improve government schools."He asked the ministry to disclose spending on government schools and the number of additional schools required to provide children with reasonable access to quality education.The six questions raised by Dipke are:Dipke's questions came against the backdrop of concerns over basic facilities in government schools. In his letter, he said children in many government schools still lack access to safe drinking water, functional washrooms and proper classrooms, while some reportedly do not even have basic benches to sit on."The visuals emerging from government schools and circulating on social media should make all of us deeply concerned. No child in this country should be forced to study in such conditions. They are being treated worse than animals," he said.He argued that improving public education should be treated as an urgent priority and called for schools to be improved "on a war footing". At the same time, he said the public should first be given a clear picture of the existing situation.Dipke stressed that his questions were not aimed at any particular political party or government."This is not about politics or any one government. This is about the future of our children," he said, adding that every child deserves "a safe classroom, clean drinking water, a functional washroom, a bench to sit on, and a teacher to teach them."He urged the ministry to make the requested information public and take urgent measures to ensure that inadequate infrastructure does not deny children access to dignified education.

Dipke posed six questions to the ministers regarding the condition and facilities inside the government schools. He also asked them to publicly disclose details on infrastructure, teacher vacancies, funding, digital facilities and the workload of teaching staff.

Article Title: 'Monstrous, mindless': Chidambaram criticises 'One Nation, One Election' plan at House panel meet
Article Text:
Former union minister P Chidambaram opposes the proposed ‘One Nation, One Election’ framework. Photo credit: ANI

NEW DELHI: Former union minister P Chidambaram has opposed the proposed ‘One Nation, One Election’ framework before a joint parliamentary committee, calling the initiative “unconstitutional”, “monstrous” and “mindless”.Chidambaram, who appeared before the panel examining the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024, argued that synchronising Lok Sabha and state assembly elections could violate the constitutional framework governing elected legislatures.Sources, quoted by news agency PTI, said the former home and finance minister told the panel that since legislatures are elected for five-year terms, curtailing their tenure would amount to a violation of the basic structure of the Constitution.Chidambaram also said his conscience did not allow him to support the proposed legislation and argued that the government does not have the required two-thirds majority to pass the bills, sources told PTI.The Congress leader described the proposal to hold nationwide elections simultaneously as a “mindless” exercise and strongly opposed the government’s push for simultaneous polls.Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Sagarika Ghosh, who is also a member of the committee, separately opposed the bills.Ghosh said the proposal could give “unbridled” power to the Election Commission, sources said.The joint committee, headed by BJP MP PP Chaudhary, also heard representations from around 10 Padma awardees, including Tarlochan Singh, Navin Khanna, Meenakshi Jain and Niru Kumar. While some supported simultaneous elections, others opposed the proposal, warning that it could lead to “chaos” in the country.The two bills were introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and subsequently referred to the joint committee for detailed examination.The proposal followed recommendations from a high-level committee headed by former president Ram Nath Kovind, which suggested holding Lok Sabha, state assembly and local body elections simultaneously in a phased manner. Union Home Minister Amit Shah was also a member of the panel.India had earlier held Lok Sabha and state assembly elections together from 1951-52 through 1967. The cycle was disrupted after premature dissolutions of some state assemblies in 1968 and 1969, followed by the early dissolution of the Fourth Lok Sabha in 1970 and fresh general elections in 1971.Since then, staggered election cycles have become the norm, with several Lok Sabha and state assembly terms ending before their full five-year tenure.
Article Summary: Former union minister P Chidambaram has opposed the proposed ‘One Nation, One Election’ framework before a joint parliamentary committee. He called the initiative ‘unconstitutional’, “monstrous” and “mindless’ The proposal followed recommendations from a high-level committee headed by former president Ram Nath Kovind.

Article Title: 'Insult to 4cr people of Telangana': CM Revanth Reddy flays Centre over US visit block
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy on Monday accused the Centre of "insulting" 4 crore people of the state by declining permission for his visit to the United States.Reddy claimed that the move showed the "Centre's discrimination" against Telangana and said that the issue would be raised in Parliament."The ministry of external affairs examined my proposal and declined clearance from the political angle. I want to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi: if there was nothing political about my foreign tour, why was permission granted for England but denied for the US?"He also questioned why Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel was allowed to visit the US and Canada from August 17 to 24 as part of the Vibrant Gujarat 2047 initiative to attract investments, while his proposed US visit under Telangana Rising 2047 was rejected."Not just America but any country in the world. If they are going to come and invest in my state, whatever regulations are made by the government of India, we want to welcome everyone, we want to protect their investment, we will make sure to get profit from Telangana, so this is very simple. This is the only political reason Narendra Modi has refused to let me travel to the US to promote Telangana," Reddy added.Reddy's remarks came days after the ministry of external affairs denied him permission to visit the United States, saying that the programme submitted for the trip was not considered appropriate to the office he holds and the purpose of the visit.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, in a briefing, said that visits by chief ministers and other dignitaries are assessed by the ministry before political clearance is granted."Let me say that the visit of chief ministers, as indeed of other dignitaries, are assessed by the ministry of external affairs in order to accord political clearance," Jaiswal said."The programme proposed, in such cases, should be appropriate to the office held and the purpose of the visit. In this particular case, that was not so in respect of the United States, and therefore the clearance was denied," he said.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister Revanth Reddy accused the Centre of "insulting" 4 crore people of the state by declining permission for his visit to the United States. Reddy claimed that the move showed the "Centre's discrimination" against Telangana and said that the issue would be raised in Parliament.

Article Title: MK Stalin moves HC against TVK MLA VS Babu's Kolathur win, seeks recount
Article Text:
DMK chief MK Stalin moves Madras High Court challenging TVK candidate VS Babu's victory in Kolathur

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK president MK Stalin on Monday moved the Madras high court challenging the victory of TVK candidate VS Babu from Kolathur in the assembly elections.In his petition, Stalin alleged malfunctions in voting machines and irregularities involving VVPAT machines, and sought an order for a recount of votes in the Kolathur constituency.Stalin also sought a declaration that Babu's election be declared void and that he himself be declared the winner.In the Tamil Nadu Assembly polls, Babu defeated Stalin by a margin of 8,795 votes.Following the results, VS Babu attributed his victory to party chief Vijay and his local connection. Touching upon the anti-incumbency factor, Babu said that his win came against the backdrop of people's desire for change in Tamil Nadu."I have won only with our leader. Our leader's face is the face of Tamil Nadu. People wanted a change, and they have changed this. I was born and brought up in that area. We know the pulse of people. It's we who made him (MK Stalin) enter Kolathur," Babu had told news agency ANI after his victory."He doesn't know anyone in Kolathur. Whether he is CM or MLA, he should mingle with the local people first. People are watching it," he had added.Stalin was a three-time MLA from Kolathur but could not retain the seat for a fourth consecutive term. Despite the setback, Stalin thanked voters, noting that the DMK alliance secured over 1.54 crore votes, with a narrow 3.52 percent difference from the winning party.
Article Summary: DMK chief MK Stalin moves Madras High Court challenging TVK candidate VS Babu's victory in Kolathur. Stalin alleged malfunctions in voting machines and irregularities involving VVPAT machines. Babu defeated Stalin by a margin of 8,795 votes.

A fresh threat letter was allegedly circulated on social media targeting Kashmiri Pandit employees serving in the Kashmir Valley, prompting the All PM Package Employees Forum Kashmir to seek enhanced security from the Jammu and Kashmir administration.In a letter to chief secretary of Jammu and Kashmir on Monday, the forum said the purported threat poster, allegedly issued by an outfit calling itself the United Liberation Council (ULC) and dated August 23, contains the names, addresses and vehicle numbers of some employees.The forum said the authenticity of the poster has not yet been verified by police or security agencies but warned that its repeated circulation was a matter of “grave concern”. In its letter, the forum said, "The authenticity of the poster is yet to be verified by the Police and security agencies. However, the repeated circulation of such threat letters and posters, particularly those containing sensitive personal information, is a matter of grave concern.One Kashmiri Pandit employee said the threats would not force them to leave the Valley. “We will neither be scared nor run away this time.Kashmir is ours also. It is our birthplace,” the employee told ANI.The employee said a similar threat letter had surfaced earlier this month and urged authorities to investigate the source of the latest threats and how the alleged perpetrators obtained sensitive personal information.The forum, citing previous targeted attacks on Kashmiri Pandit employees, sought immediate security cover, a review of arrangements at workplaces and residences, and protection for employees whose personal details may have appeared in the alleged poster.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Monday issued summons to commentator Abhijit Iyer-Mitra and several media platforms in a suit filed by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das , who has alleged that his residential address and other personal details were published on social media without his consent.The development came during the hearing of Das's plea seeking interim protection against the alleged disclosure of his personal information. The court was informed that X, formerly known as Twitter, had removed the posts allegedly carrying Das's residential address.Justice Sachin Datta issued notice on Das's application seeking interim relief and directed the defendants to file their replies. The matter will next be heard on September 14.Senior Advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for Das, submitted that personnel of The Pamphlet had entered his client's residential property without permission and recorded a video.Sibal alleged that Iyer-Mitra subsequently added to the video and shared it on social media. He further submitted that some posts on X specifically mentioned Das's residential address.Seeking protection for his client, Sibal urged the court to ensure that the posts, which had already been removed by X under its policy, were not restored.Appearing for X, counsel told the court that the concerned links were "no longer accessible." The submission was recorded by the court.Counsel for The Pamphlet also submitted that the posts were no longer available on X and sought time to respond to the allegations on merits.The court further allowed Das to correct the name of The Sunday Guardian in the proceedings and permitted him to amend the memo of parties and plaint within three days.Apart from Iyer-Mitra and The Pamphlet, the suit names LawBeat, The Jaipur Dialogues, The Sunday Guardian, Google LLC and X Corp as defendants.Das has sought permanent and mandatory injunctions against the defendants, besides damages, alleging violation of his privacy, dignity and security.In his plea, Das alleged that his residential address and other personal details were recorded and circulated without his consent. He claimed that the disclosure of his exact address could expose him and other occupants of his residence to security risks.Das further alleged that representatives of The Pamphlet entered the residential premises where he lives and recorded videos of the property, including its interiors, which were later posted on X.His plea also claimed that he had faced threats and targeted hostility in the past because of his journalistic work, public-interest disclosures and political activities.During the hearing, Das's counsel emphasised the potential security implications of making a person's residential details publicly available and sought continued protection against any restoration or further circulation of the allegedly offending posts.The court, however, has not yet adjudicated the allegations on the merits. The defendants have been given an opportunity to file their responses.The matter will next come up before the Delhi High Court on September 14.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court summons Abhijit Iyer-Mitra, media portals over alleged disclosure of Saurav Das's address. Court was informed that X, formerly known as Twitter, had removed the posts allegedly carrying Das's residential address. The matter will next be heard on September 14.

NEW DELHI: A political row erupted between the BJP and Congress over an alleged fish feast organised during a welcome programme for newly appointed Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai in Ayodhya.The controversy erupted after a video surfaced showing fish being prepared at a banquet hall in Ayodhya, where a welcome programme for the Congress leader was being held.Several local religious figures objected to the food arrangements, saying the programme was taking place during the holy month of Sawan.Reacting to the controversy, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused Ajay Rai of “duplicity” over the alleged fish feast.“You saw the behaviour of the Congress state president: he goes to offer prayers at Hanumangarhi, but later outside he enjoys a feast of fish. He could have eaten whatever he wanted outside—anywhere other than Ayodhya. Yet, this is the duplicity they display. Even a chameleon would be put to shame by these people; it would wonder what kind of human species this is—chanting 'Ram-Ram' inside the temple and feasting on fish the moment they step out.This is their history—the history of this Congress state president," Yogi said.BJP MLA Ved Prakash Gupta criticised the Congress over the alleged fish feast, saying, “scores of Hindus are immersed in the worship of Lord Shiva during Sawan. Organising a fish feast at such a time is an open display of Congress’ anti-Hindu mindset.”He alleged that visiting temples in Ayodhya and then attending an event where fish was served exposed the Congress party’s “dual standards”.UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary described the event as “highly condemnable and unforgivable” and demanded that the Congress publicly apologise to saints and devotees.Responding to the controversy Ajay Rai denied any involvement in the food arrangements and challenged Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to provide evidence."The CM is criticising; does the CM have any photos? If he can produce any pictures, I will be ready to resign immediately. Nishad Samaj invited me to a program in Ayodhya yesterday. If they were getting fish prepared there, it would be their concern. I attended the program and returned," Rai said.Congress MP Pawan Khera criticised the Bharatiya Janata Party, saying that such controversies were being raised to divert attention from more pressing issues, including paper leaks."Such issues are raised so that important issues like paper leaks are not raised. Today, when people think of Ayodhya, they are reminded of the theft of donations. Can 'Maach-Bhaat' make people forget about the theft of donations in Ayodhya? People in Nagpur think fish should not be consumed. Ajay Rai is a vegetarian, even if he were not, what is wrong with it?" Khera said.Ajay Rai had earlier defended the event, saying it was organised by members of the Nishad community, for whom fish forms an important part of their food culture.“Yeh Nishad samaj ka karyakram tha. Nishad samaj machhli ka vyapar karta hai. Unke liye machhli sabse achha bhojan hai jo woh kisi ko de sakte hain… and how can one check a host from cooking what they want,” Rai said.He also questioned the allegation that his presence at the event amounted to a violation of Sanatan traditions. “Where is the proof that I violated Sanatan tradition?” he asked.Rai also hit back at the criticism by drawing a comparison with BJP leaders. Referring to BJP national president Nitin Nabin and an earlier controversy involving non-vegetarian food, he said, “Nitin Nabin consumed non-vegetarian food in Andhra Pradesh and claimed that he had eaten jackfruit. They are treating me with the same lens.”
Article Summary: The controversy erupted after a video surfaced showing fish being prepared at a banquet hall in Ayodhya. Local religious figures objected to the food arrangements, saying the programme was taking place during the holy month of Sawan. Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath accused Ajay Rai of ‘duplicity’ over the alleged fish feast.

NEW DELHI: Several houses were set ablaze and a CRPF jawan was later injured in a gunfight between two groups in Manipur ’s Senapati district on Monday, police said.According to a senior officer, houses were set ablaze after miscreants torched a house in Taphou Kuki village in Kangpokpi district around 2:30 am.“Following the incident of arson in Kangpokpi, several houses were burnt at Naga Taphou in Senapati district at 4 am. NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal on Thursday turned the heat on Punjab 's ruling AAP and main opposition party the Congress over the sensitive issue of sacrilege, or "beadbi", claiming that the state had witnessed more than 600 such incidents over the past decade.The SAD MP also acknowledged and apologised for one sacrilege incident that took place during the Shiromani Akali Dal's tenure in Punjab.She said, "Unfortunately, one incident of Beadbi happened during our tenure and we are very sorry for it. We have vowed that until we punish the perpetrators, we will not rest."Targeting the AAP and Congress, Harsimrat said, " But what about the Aam Aadmi Party and the Congress that politicised this sensitive issue. What about the 600+ beadbis which have happened in the last 10 years. What about the people who swore on Gutka Sahab and promised to end the drug trade."She further said, "What about those who gave guarantees of giving justice in Beadbi cases in the first 4 months? Why is no one asking them for answers? Why aren’t you holding them accountable?!"Harsimrat also targeted the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government and appealed to the people of Punjab to end the "remote control rule" of the state from Delhi."Punjab is for Punjabis," the former Union minister said, adding that restoring peace and communal harmony, tackling gangster rule and ending the drug menace would be the top priorities of the SAD if it returned to power.She was addressing a party conference held to mark the 41st martyrdom anniversary of Sant Harchand Singh Longowal.Referring to the recent attack on SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal in Maharashtra's Nanded, Harsimrat said her husband would not be intimidated by those who had attacked him twice.She also urged Punjabis to get rid of what she called "divisive forces" that were looting the state and destroying the future of its youth.Urging people to consider why Sukhbir Badal was being attacked in 'Gurughar', she said that "it is clear this is being done by cowards who have become stooges of governments".She said the SAD had always prioritised peace, communal harmony and the development of Punjab, which, according to her, had not gone down well with its opponents. She accused them of trying to weaken and split the party by encouraging fringe elements.Calling the attack on the SAD president inside a gurdwara against the principles of Sikhism, Harsimrat said, "Yes, as a wife and a mother, I did get scared for a moment, but today I can strongly look you in the eyes and assert we are all not scared and never will be."She said this resolve had unsettled SAD's opponents, who had realised that Sukhbir Badal was in "chardikala" (in high spirits) and would continue to follow in the footsteps of his father and former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal by working for communal harmony and the welfare of Punjabis.
Article Summary: Harsimrat claims 'over 600 beadbis' took place in a decade in Punjab. SAD MP also apologised for one sacrilege incident that took place during the Shiromani Akali Dal's tenure. She was addressing a party conference held to mark the 41st martyrdom anniversary of Sant Harchand Singh Longowal.

We had gone our separate ways over the farm laws," Majithia told ANI.He then listed reasons why he believes people want the two parties to reunite, while making it clear that the final decision would rest with the leaderships of both parties."But considering Punjab's situation as a border state, social harmony and the social fabric, people want the two parties to come together. Whether they will come together will be decided by the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal leadership. Harsimrat Badal has expressed the people’s sentiments. What the outcome will be, only time will tell," he said.Majithia was referring to recent cryptic remarks byHarsimrat Kaur Badal , the SAD's only Lok Sabha MP and wife of party chief Sukhbir Singh Badal."It is not my duty to speak, so I am holding back my tongue. You will come to know yourself.May God bless and may people give us strength. Such agreements, by way of which works related to development and progress used to be carried out from Delhi, and once again, the foundation of that development and progress is being laid in Punjab, which benefits the people of Punjab and Punjab," she said on Thursday.The SAD first joined the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 1998. However, it left the alliance in 2020 in protest against the BJP-led Centre's contentious farm laws, which were eventually withdrawn in 2021.Earlier this month, Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi, sparking speculation about the possibility of a reunion of the former allies.The two parties governed Punjab together from 2007 to 2017.
Article Summary: Bikram Singh Majithia says people in Punjab want the SAD and the BJP to come together. He says the final decision would rest with the leaderships of both parties. SAD first joined the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 1998. The two parties governed Punjab together from 2007 to 2017.

Article Title: 'Over 200 pellets in body, lost his eye': Rahul Gandhi sits on dharna with victim; seeks FIR
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi on dharna outside DCP office along with pellet gun victim

What Congress claims

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Friday staged protest outside Parliament Street Police Station, demanding justice for pellet-gun victims in police crackdown during student protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Priyanka Gandhi also joined Rahul Gandhi staging a 'dharna' at the Sansad Marg Police Station.Former Congress chief met senior police officials at DCP office in Connaught Place.He sought registration of a complaint over police action and excessive use of force, including the use of pellet guns, against student protesters during a demonstration over NEET irregularities on July 20.Rahul has said he will remain at the police station and continue to seek justice until the complaint is formally registered.Speaking to reporters outside Parliament Street Police Station, Rahul Gandhi displayed a pellet and alleged that more than 200 pellets were lodged in the body of student protester Sahil Lochav."Look at this pellet carefully. This is a pellet. Where did these pellets come from? They came from his (Sahil Lochav) body. Look at these pellets lodged in his body. There are more than 200 pellets in his body. These are AIIMS and Lady Hardinge Hospital reports, which clearly state that there are more than 200 pellets in his body.There are three pellets in his eye, and he has lost vision in that eye. He will not be able to see through that eye. There are also pellets lodged very close to his heart, which cannot be removed," Rahul said."Delhi Police has said that they did not fire the pellets. So, there is only one question: If you did not fire them, then someone must have fired these pellets. Perhaps someone else fired them at him. And if no one else fired them, then perhaps he fired the pellets at himself," he added.Rahul had earlier visited Mandir Marg Police Station and requested that a case be registered. After police allegedly declined to register the complaint, he proceeded to meet the DCP Central.Earlier on July 25, Rahul Gandhi had directly criticised Union home minister Amit Shah, holding him responsible for the use of excessive force, including pellet guns, against student protesters in the national capital.Speaking at a press conference, Rahul alleged that Shah had authorised the use of lethal weapons during the protests and said the issue was of fundamental importance in Parliament.Congress said in a statement that Delhi Police had refused to register an FIR over a pellet gun attack on student protester Sahil Lochav, saying the matter had been raised with the police earlier but no case had been registered.The party said Lochav had submitted a written complaint to Delhi Police on August 14 in the presence of his lawyers, but police did not provide an I/O number or an acknowledgement. The matter was followed up again on August 17 through email and phone calls, but the party alleged that no I/O number was provided.Congress said Rahul Gandhi later accompanied Lochav to the DCP office to press for registration of the case. The party alleged that the DCP did not provide the name of the investigating officer or the I/O number.“As it’s a cognisable offence, a FIR also has to be registered, but Delhi police not doing so,” Congress said.“No FIR. No justice. So we sit,” Congress said, referring to Rahul’s sit-in with Lochav outside the DCP office.“This is not delay. This is denial of justice. We will not leave until an FIR is filed,” the party added.On July 20, thousands of students took part in a Parliament march organised by the CJP, demanding, among other things, the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination paper leaks and reforms in the examination system.As protesters attempted to march towards Parliament and cross police barricades in central Delhi, security personnel used tear gas and lathi-charge to disperse the crowd. Several videos later circulated on social media, showing police personnel manhandling protesters, leading to allegations of excessive use of force.The Delhi Police, however, defended its action, saying force was used only after sections of the protesting crowd allegedly turned violent and resorted to stone-pelting.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi staged protest outside Parliament Street Police Station, demanding justice for pellet-gun victims in police crackdown during student protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20. Priyanka Gandhi also joined Rahul Gandhi staging a 'dharna' at the Sansad Marg Police Station.

Article Title: Who is Jed York’s wife Danielle Belluomini? Everything to know about the 49ers owner’s longtime partner
Article Text:
Who is Danielle Belluomini, Jed York ’s wife?

Jed York and Danielle Belluomini’s marriage takes a new turn

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The arrest of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York has put his private life under an unusually bright spotlight. While the legal case in Ohio has quickly moved toward resolution, another detail has drawn attention: his marriage to Danielle Belluomini. The couple married in 2011 and have two sons, but their relationship has largely remained away from the public eye. Recent court records now add a major new chapter to their story.Danielle Belluomini has built a life far removed from the constant attention that comes with owning an NFL franchise. Before marrying York, she worked as a sixth-grade science teacher in a San Francisco public school. The two reportedly began dating during that period, long before York became one of the most prominent figures in professional football.The couple married in 2011. Their first son, Jaxon, was born in October 2012, followed later by their second son, Brixton. For years, Belluomini rarely appeared in the news unless she was accompanying York at an official 49ers or NFL event.One such appearance came at the 2017 NFL Honors in Houston, where she joined York on the red carpet. Photos from the event offered a glimpse of a family that generally kept its personal life private.Belluomini has also maintained a limited social media presence. Her Instagram account is private, while her X account has seen little activity in recent years. That low profile has made her personal life difficult to track compared with the highly public career of her husband.The picture surrounding the couple changed significantly in 2026. According to court documents cited by the San Francisco Chronicle and SFGATE, York filed for divorce from Danielle in Santa Clara County Superior Court on May 11. The filing cited “irreconcilable differences.” Danielle later responded in court, and the dissolution case remained pending as of the latest reported court records.That detail is important because York’s Ohio arrest came only a few months after the divorce filing. On August 23, he was arrested in East Palestine during an operation involving local police and the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force. He was initially accused of engaging in prostitution after authorities said he had responded to an online advertisement and arranged a $140 sexual encounter.The legal outcome, however, was different from the original accusation. York pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after the prostitution charge was amended. He received a jail sentence covering time served and was ordered to pay $1,150 in fines.The 49ers have kept their response brief, saying, “As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time.”For Danielle Belluomini, the renewed attention is striking because she has spent much of her adult life outside the spotlight. Her story is less about celebrity than privacy, family and a marriage that is now being examined publicly because of events surrounding one of America's best-known sports owners.
Article Summary: Jed York filed for divorce from Danielle Belluomini on May 11. The filing cited “irreconcilable differences” The couple married in 2011 and have two sons. York pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Article Title: "Erika was photographed over his bloody mic": Candace Owens fires another shot at Erika Kirk as Tyler Bowyer’s Lindsay Clancy post sparks outrage
Article Text:
Candace Owens (Image via Getty)

Candace Owens challenges Tyler Bowyer over Erika Kirk comparison

Erika Kirk and Lindsay Clancy controversy intensifies

Candace Owens has sharply pushed back against a post by Turning Point USA chief operating officer Tyler Bowyer, who compared the public treatment of Erika Kirk with the support shown to Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy during her murder trial. Owens argued that criticism of fundraising efforts for Clancy can exist alongside criticism of TPUSA’s handling of Charlie Kirk’s death, adding another tense chapter to her long-running clash with the organization.The dispute began after Bowyer used X to contrast the backlash faced by Erika Kirk with the financial support surrounding Clancy’s legal case.His post stated, “strangle your three kids while evading your mental illness: ONE MILLION DOLLARS”.He then wrote, “lose your husband & father of your children but carry an organization with millions of followers on your back that recruits & registers young Patriots: A LIFETIME OF HARASSMENT”.Owens reposted Bowyer’s comments but rejected the comparison. She pointed to the commercial and fundraising activity surrounding Erika after Charlie Kirk’s death and questioned whether TPUSA should be weighing in on Clancy’s case at all.“You guys sold 50,000 t-shirts at the “event of the century” as Erika walked out to sparklers. You raised 40 million in one night at Mar-A-Lago as Erika was photographed over his bloody mic. It’s possible to disagree with fundraisers for Lindsay Clancy and also think TPUSA should sit this one out entirely.”Her response is significant because Owens has repeatedly criticized Erika Kirk and Turning Point USA since Charlie Kirk was killed. Rather than treating the controversy as a simple argument over Clancy, Owens has continued to use public posts to challenge how TPUSA has responded to the aftermath of Charlie’s death.The comparison comes as Clancy faces three murder charges in Massachusetts over the deaths of her children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months. She has pleaded not guilty.The case has also raised difficult questions about mental illness and criminal responsibility. If convicted, Clancy could face life in prison without parole. A finding of not guilty because of a lack of criminal responsibility could instead result in commitment to a state mental health facility.Meanwhile, Owens has continued questioning Erika Kirk publicly on several fronts. She has criticized Erika’s interactions with journalist Brandy Zadrozny, challenged the privacy surrounding Charlie Kirk’s burial location and raised broader questions about the events following his death.Charlie Kirk, 31, was fatally shot on September 10, 2025, during a student question-and-answer event at Utah Valley University in Orem, according to the university’s account of the shooting. Tyler Robinson has been accused in the killing.The latest exchange shows that the conflict surrounding Charlie Kirk’s legacy is far from settled. Owens’ response has shifted attention back toward the conduct of TPUSA itself, while Bowyer’s original post sought to highlight what he described as a stark difference in public sympathy. With both sides continuing to speak publicly, the controversy is likely to remain a major point of discussion among Kirk supporters and Owens’ audience.
Article Summary: Candace Owens has sharply pushed back against a post by Turning Point USA chief operating officer Tyler Bowyer. Bowyer compared the public treatment of Erika Kirk with the support shown to Massachusetts mother Lindsay Clancy during her murder trial. Owens argued that criticism of fundraising efforts for Clancy can exist alongside criticism of TPUSA’s handling of Charlie Kirk's death.

Article Title: ‘We can drive them crazy’: Rahul Gandhi takes aim at PM Modi, Amit Shah

Rahul addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress

In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them.
