Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: In 2016, Mark Zuckerberg's wife Priscilla Chan founded a school that was designed to be different; 10 years later and after $125 million funding, Board voted to close it
Article Text:
Why the board voted to close school founded by Priscilla Chan

A mixed academic record

Impact on families

What CZI is providing as the school winds down

Priscilla Chan's hands-on role

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg ’s wife Dr. Priscilla Chan, co-founded The Primary School in East Palo Alto, California in 2016. The school was designed to serve the low-income families. The tuition-free private school aimed to support the “whole child” through wraparound services such as dental checkups, wellness coaching, and early-intervention screenings. For more than ten years the school received more than $125 million from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI). However, despite the strong support services and community engagement, academic performance often fell short of state norms, complicating efforts to replicate the model in public and charter schools. A report by Wall Street Journal revealed that despite all these efforts the school shut its doors this past June after a decade of operation.The Primary School's board voted unanimously in April 2025 to close the school after learning that CZI would not continue funding it beyond the 2025-26 academic year, according to people familiar with the situation. Board president Jean-Claude Brizard said he had presented CZI with several options for the school's future before the vote, including winding the school down gradually, and said the board would not have voted to close without alignment from its primary funder.A CZI spokesperson said the decision to close ultimately rested with the school's board, and that the organization's focus had been on the school's academic results rather than cost.The closure reflects a broader shift within CZI, which has moved its philanthropic focus away from social issues and toward scientific research in recent years.By some measures, the Primary School's academic performance fell short of both state benchmarks and its own leadership's expectations, complicating efforts to eventually replicate its model in public and charter schools elsewhere. A Stanford University report found that in spring 2025, 14% of local third-grade-and-above students exceeded state literacy standards, compared to 26% at the Primary School itself and 47% statewide. Still, the school said its eighth-grade students, many of whom had attended for a decade, demonstrated above 50% grade-level proficiency in their final year, and a founding staff member said students showed steady academic progress after the pandemic, alongside improvements in wellbeing and socio-emotional skills. Around 85% of Primary School students completed their annual well-child visit, compared to 55% of children on Medicaid in the county.Around 540 children were enrolled across the two campuses of the Primary School. As per the WSJ report, Mele Fakapelea, whose daughter Telesia won a lottery spot in the school's founding class before Fakapelea enrolled four younger children as well, described it as "a godsend school," and said losing its support system felt devastating. On the other hand, Angelica Cardenas, whose 3-year-old daughter and five nieces and nephews were enrolled, said she learned about the closure through the news rather than directly from the school, arguing that families should have been told sooner if funding was going to end. After the shut down of the Primary School founded by Priscilla Chan, the students will be absorbed in the Ravenswood City Elementary School District. The school is also preparing for an enrollment surge and renovating a campus to avoid placing students in portable trailers.CZI pledged $50 million when the closure was announced, covering the remaining balance of the school's lease with the district and supporting local organizations to continue offering some services. The organization also contributed $3.6 million toward education savings accounts for affected families: $10,000 per elementary student, $2,500 per preschooler, and $1,000 for children in early-childhood education programs.Chan served as the Primary School's co-founder and board chair for about eight years, until 2023, with CZI functioning as its main funder throughout. According to CZI, having a single major backer indefinitely was never the intended long-term model; the goal had been a school that could eventually be sustained primarily through public investment, and the school reportedly tried to keep its per-pupil spending in line with typical public school levels. Brizard said Chan actively lobbied her network to bring in additional funding sources, though attracting outside donors proved difficult given the perception of a school already backed by one of the world's wealthiest individuals.Chan was known to be candid about her frustration with the school's academic outcomes, telling the Journal last year that results weren't where anyone would have wanted them to be. Brizard said the timing of CZI's broader strategic shift, which staff were told about in early 2025 shortly after Zuckerberg and Chan attended President Trump's inauguration, and the board's subsequent vote to close was coincidental; CZI said there was no evidence the inauguration had influenced the board's decision.
Article Summary: Priscilla Chan co-founded The Primary School in East Palo Alto, California in 2016. The tuition-free private school aimed to support the “whole child” through wraparound services such as dental checkups, wellness coaching, and early- intervention screenings. For more than ten years the school received more than $125 million from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.

Article Title: Steve Hanke, who has been a teacher at Johns Hopkins University for almost 60 years says that he is fine students using AI to cheat, because he can easily ...
Article Text:
A former Ivy League admissions dean agrees to Steve Hanke

How some teachers are responding

Steve Hanke, who has taught applied economics at Johns Hopkins University for nearly 60 years, recently told Business Insider that he has “absolutely no problem with AI and students.” Hanke, who also served on President Reagan’s Council of Economic Advisers, described himself as an “old fox” who finds it “very easy” to differentiate between student work and chatbot-generated output. Hanke noted that what he sees as the poor writing skills of today’s students, even at elite universities, as one of the main reason AI subscribers stand out. It’s blatant when a student submission has been generated by AI,” he said, adding that his familiarity with students’ knowledge of economics makes it “pretty easy to spot” when work doesn’t match their skill level.“The only problem that AI poses is that it requires the old fox to be on guard, more than would have been the case sans AI,” Hanke explained. He emphasized that vigilance is the key to catching AI misuse in academic work.Drusilla Blackman, a former dean of admissions at both Harvard and Columbia, echoed Hanke's assessment in a separate interview with Business Insider. Blackman said it's almost always evident to an educator when a student has used AI, since the submitted work tends not to match that student's typical standard of writing or critical thinking.She said work that is clearly disproportionate to what a student would normally produce is detectable. Blackman is the founder of Deans of Admissions, a group that advises families on getting their children into top universities in the US and Britain.Beyond simply detecting AI-generated submissions after the fact, Business Insider reported last year that several teachers had begun taking a more defensive approach, redesigning assignments specifically to resist AI use, and in some cases returning to handwritten assignments altogether to discourage students from relying on chatbots in the first place.
Article Summary: Steve Hanke, who has taught applied economics at Johns Hopkins University for nearly 60 years, recently told Business Insider that he has “absolutely no problem with AI and students” Drusilla Blackman, a former dean of admissions at both Harvard and Columbia, echoed Hanke's assessment in a separate interview with Business Insider.

Article Title: Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley on people vandalising Flock cameras across America: When people talk about only privacy, they are forgetting that ...
Article Text:
Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley said the debate should not focus on privacy or safety alone

Flock Safety faces growing privacy concerns

How Flock responded

Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley has called for a balance between privacy and public safety as his company faces growing criticism over its surveillance technology, including reports of Flock cameras being vandalised across the US. Garrett Langley said the debate should not focus on privacy or safety alone, arguing that the country needs to find a compromise between the two. His comments come as concerns grow over how Flock's cameras, drones and license plate recognition technology could be used by law enforcement and other agencies.“When people talk about just one of these, privacy or safety, they’re prioritizing the wrong thing, and what we have to prioritize as a country is compromise,” Garrett Langley said during a recent interview with Fox News. “How do we have our safety, and how do we balance privacy?”Flock Safety has faced increasing scrutiny over its surveillance technology. Critics have raised concerns that the company's cameras and data could be misused. The concerns have also been linked to alleged cases of improper use by police officers. The Washington Post recently identified 46 cases in which police officers were accused of using Flock technology without authorization, including allegations involving the stalking of wives, girlfriends or former partners.After hearing from one of the alleged victims, Langley told CBS News, “I apologize.It kills me that she went through that.”However, he also defended the company's role in identifying misuse. “I don’t think that Flock created police abuse. I think we’re the first company to ever shine a light on it and build the tools to find it,” he said.Flock has responded by reducing its default data retention period from 30 days to seven days and requiring a case code before users can access data. However, these settings can be overridden in certain situations, including through a feature called Evidence Mode.Langley has also called for stronger rules around illegal use of surveillance data. “Today, it is too often that in Flock and in other technologies, there’s no regulation. There’s no accountability, and we think that’s wrong,” he said.
Article Summary: Flock Safety has faced increasing scrutiny over its surveillance technology. Critics have raised concerns that the company's cameras and data could be misused. The concerns have also been linked to alleged cases of improper use by police officers. CEO Garrett Langley said the debate should not focus on privacy or safety alone.

Article Title: '12th pass vs Boston University': Kangana Ranaut takes dig at Abhijeet Dipke with English comparison reel
Article Text:
Kangana Ranaut shared an Instagram reel contrasting her English speaking with Abhijeet Dipke's

Kangana Ranaut instagram story





NEW DELHI: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut has taken an apparent swipe at Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) founder Abhijeet Dipke by sharing an Instagram reel that compares their English-speaking abilities and contrasts clips of the two speaking in English.The reel, shared by Kangana on her Instagram Story, opens with Dipke delivering a public statement in English before cutting to a video of Kangana speaking in English about how she was perceived as a female actor in the film industry.The caption on the reel read, ‘12th pass Kangana Ranaut vs Boston University CJP Dipke English level: One is fire, the other needs a reboot.’Kangana has previously spoken about struggling with English early in her acting career.Recalling an appearance on Koffee With Karan , where she said she was mocked by actor Sonam Kapoor, Kangana later reflected on the experience.“What I learned from years of fights with film mafia is that no outsider will ever be mocked for not speaking English…also that show is officially closed forever.”She also wrote, “Please don't miss my comeback in the end. Even at 24 after being openly bullied, humiliated and mocked I showed grace sophistication articulation and humility which English speaking gossipy aunties with so called great upbringing can never…”Dipke had also addressed questions about his English-speaking skills on Instagram Stories on Sunday.Responding to a follower who asked why he hesitates while speaking English, he said he becomes conscious when facing the camera.Kangana has previously criticised protests associated with the CJP and also questioned Dipke’s age and his claim of being a student.“I googled this person and he is 28 years old. How he claims to be a student I have no clue! Yes I am in politics for past 2 years but I have been in public life for the last 20 years. At his age, I had 2 National Awards.”Reflecting on her own experience as a first-time MP, Kangana said she initially found the workload overwhelming, citing her roles as a filmmaker, performing artist, producer, screenwriter and entrepreneur.
Article Summary: Kangana Ranaut shared an Instagram reel contrasting her English speaking with Abhijeet Dipke's. The reel opens with Dipke delivering a public statement in English. It then cuts to a video of Kangana speaking in English about how she was perceived as a female actor.

Article Title: ‘Food not tasty enough’: 2 minors stab hotel worker in northeast Delhi; held
Article Text:
Authorities initiated legal proceedings under attempted murder and common intention charges (Representative image)





NEW DELHI: Two minors were apprehended for allegedly stabbing a 25-year-old hotel worker with a kitchen knife following an argument over the taste of food in northeast Delhi’s Kabutar Market. The injured man was identified as Ehasan, a local resident.According to police, the incident took place at 9pm Friday. Ehasan was taken to Jag Pravesh Chandra Hospital by his neighbour and was later referred to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital for further treatment.During the preliminary inquiry, police learnt from the hotel owner that Ehasan was on duty when two customers allegedly got into an argument with him over the taste of the food they had ordered. The duo allegedly attacked him with a sharp-edged weapon before fleeing.A case was registered under Sections 109 (attempt to murder) and 3(5) (common intention) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at Welcome police station.A senior police officer said, “Following technical and field investigation, the two were traced and apprehended.”Police said both suspects were found to be minors, aged 14 and 15. During questioning, they allegedly admitted their involvement in the incident. The vegetable-cutting knife used in the attack was also seized.Police are also examining the circumstances that led to the altercation and verifying the sequence of events.
Article Summary: Two minors apprehended for allegedly stabbing a 25-year-old hotel worker. Incident took place in northeast Delhi’s Kabutar Market. The injured man was identified as Ehasan, a local resident. Authorities initiated legal proceedings under attempted murder and common intention charges.

Article Title: SUV on rampage kills 71-year-old woman in Delhi; hits several vehicles before ramming couple
Article Text:
Shashi with husband Kulbhushan (L)

sarson ka saag





NEW DELHI: An elderly woman was killed and her husband injured after an SUV hit several vehicles before ramming the pedestrian couple near Kailash Colony metro station in Greater Kailash-1 at 6.45pm Sunday.The SUV driver, Tapan Ahir (59), was arrested on the spot. Police are examining whether any mechanical problem in the vehicle led to the crash. Ahir’s blood sample was sent to Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for alcohol screening.Shashi Bhateja (71), a retired employee of Central Public Works Department (CPWD), used to live in Lajpat Nagar with her husband, Kulbhushan Bhateja (65), a retired bank manager. She accompanied him to a dentist and was waiting with him to take an autorickshaw back home when the vehicle hit another SUV, an autorickshaw and a cycle rickshaw before ramming the couple.The Bhatejas were rushed to Moolchand Hospital, where Shashi was declared dead, said Pradeep Malhotra, her brother. Kulbhushan sustained a fracture and an eye injury. He was later declared fit to give a statement.Ahir, who has been working as a driver for a person since 1997, was on his way to pick up his brother from Kailash Colony market when the accident took place, deputy commissioner of police (south) Anant Mittal said.Eyewitnesses said that after Ahir hit an SUV, he reportedly panicked and pressed the accelerator, crashing into some concrete pillars before colliding with the auto and cycle rickshaw, which was crushed. The impact also left four pillars uprooted.Malhotra said about her sister, “Shashi was a brilliant cook and would regularly come to my house withafter my wife passed away during the pandemic. She took care of everyone, especially her grandchildren, whom she spoke to every day.”The retired CPWD employee loved travelling and had planned a pilgrimage to Ram Temple in Ayodhya with her husband in Oct. “Kulbhushan kept asking about her every two minutes while being treated in hospital. We told him about her death once he was stable,” Pradeep added.A case was registered under Sections 281 (danger or obstruction in a public way or line of navigation), 125(a) (act endangering the life or personal safety of others) and 106 (causing death by negligence) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against Ahir.
Article Summary: Shashi Bhateja (71), a retired employee of Central Public Works Department (CPWD), used to live in Lajpat Nagar with her husband. She accompanied him to a dentist and was waiting with him to take an autorickshaw back home. SUV driver, Tapan Ahir (59), was arrested on the spot. Police examining whether any mechanical problem in the vehicle led to the crash.

Article Title: BJP, Congress wary as rival Senas fight it out over Marathi rule for autos, taxis
Article Text:
Mumbai's auto and taxi driver sector has become a new political battleground.





MUMBAI: As the two Shiv Senas battle it out with the 'Marathi' rule for auto and taxi drivers brought in by Shinde Sena and the Sena (UBT)'s opposition to bike taxis, their alliance partners BJP and Congress respectively are wary and trying to do the balancing act.Political observers said the auto rickshaw and taxi drivers' space is the new battleground for the Senas as they try to score political points. However, the BJP, which enjoys support of migrant taxi and autorickshaw drivers, is upset as the compulsory Marathi diktat and introduction of bike taxis hit the conventional autorickshaw and taxi trade, political observers said."The Shinde Sena seems to have introduced the Marathi diktat to take on Sena (UBT) and MNS on their Marathi manoos plank, which helped them dent Shinde Sena in the BMC polls. So there is competition between the two Senas to woo Marathi voters, and this is being done through auto and taxi drivers. Sena (UBT) has entered this space by opposing bike taxis. But the moves by both Senas are not going down well with their alliance partners. BJP is particularly not happy with Shinde Sena as most drivers are North Indian and are BJP supporters. So this isn't going down well with them," said an observer.The Congress, which is UBT Sena's ally, has opposed strict enforcement of the Marathi rule. Mumbai Congress chief and MP Varsha Gaikwad had warned the policy threatens drivers' jobs and economic uplift. Congress MLA Nana Patole had defended linguistic freedom and said people should be allowed to speak any language they choose.Ex-MP Sanjay Nirupam on Monday urged transport minister Pratap Sarnaik to reconsider punitive action against rickshaw drivers who have not yet cleared the Marathi language requirement, arguing livelihoods should not be jeopardised.
Article Summary: The auto rickshaw and taxi drivers' space is the new battleground for the Senas as they try to score political points. The BJP, which enjoys support of migrant taxi and autorickshaw drivers, is upset as the compulsory Marathi diktat and introduction of bike taxis hit the conventional trade. But the moves by both Senas are not going down well with their alliance partners.

Article Title: 7-year-old boy ‘with fever’ dies at Palghar ashram school, 26 students in hospital
Article Text:
The death raised concerns of a possible outbreak of an infectious disease

Palghar

:





A seven-year-old student died at an ashram school in Palghar district’s Maswan on Monday, while 26 other students were hospitalised after developing symptoms such as fever and cough, raising concerns of a possible outbreak of an infectious disease.The death came barely a fortnight after three girls died of a snakebite at an ashram school in Gadchiroli district. The school has since lost its licence.The Palghar student who died, Shreyas Ambat, had been suffering from fever for two days. He attended school on Monday but his condition suddenly deteriorated and he developed breathing difficulty. He died while being taken to hospital, officials said.The ashram school has around 400 students. Health authorities screened students and admitted 26 who showed symptoms such as fever, body ache and cough to the primary healthcare centre as a precautionary measure. Their blood samples were sent to a laboratory for further testing.Dahanu tribal development project officer Vishal Khatri said the exact cause of Shreyas’s death would be known after the postmortem examination. “The students who have been hospitalised will be kept under observation for two days.”Palghar medical officer Dr Umesh Dumpalwar said preventive measures had been initiated in view of the possibility of an infectious disease outbreak.
Article Summary: Shreyas Ambat had been suffering from fever for two days. He attended school on Monday but his condition suddenly deteriorated. He died while being taken to hospital, officials said. Health authorities screened students and admitted 26 who showed symptoms such as fever, body ache and cough to the primary healthcare centre.

Article Title: Vasai labourer dies after falling from 15th floor
Article Text: Vasai: A 22-year-old labourer died after falling from the 15th floor of an under-construction 22-storey building while carrying out painting work in the Babola area of Vasai West on Sunday afternoon. The deceased has been identified as Mursalim Momin.The incident took place at the ‘Aryana’ building located behind Western Hotel in Babola. According to the police, Momin was working on the 15th floor at around noon. He reportedly fell from the building while getting down to relieve himself.He sustained severe injuries to his head, face, chin and legs and was rendered unconscious at the spot. He was immediately rushed to Sir D.M. Petit Hospital for treatment. However, he succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment.
Article Summary: The deceased has been identified as Mursalim Momin. The incident took place at the ‘Aryana’ building located behind Western Hotel in Babola. He reportedly fell from the building while getting down to relieve himself.

Article Title: Jarange rejects govt outreach, firm on Aug 29 fast; warns protest may shift to Mumbai
Article Text:
Ministers fail to break ice as Jarange remains firm on a decisive and final hunger strike from Aug 29

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Monday rejected the state’s latest attempt to dissuade him from resuming agitation, reiterating that his “decisive and final” indefinite hunger strike will begin at Antarwali Sarati on Aug 29. He also warned the protest could later move to Mumbai, including near the chief minister’s official residence, Varsha.The announcement came after senior ministers Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, Shambhuraj Desai and Uday Samant, along with BJP MLA Prasad Lad, met Jarange at Antarwali Sarati in an effort to persuade him to withdraw the proposed fast. Jarange, however, remained unmoved, saying govt had until Aug 28 to fulfil its commitments.“Now there will be no stopping. The agitation will be held on Aug 29,” Jarange said, adding that the Maratha community had grown tired of repeated assurances.The date coincides with the third anniversary of the police lathicharge at Antarwali Sarati that sparked the latest phase of the Maratha reservation movement.Jarange accused govt of delaying implementation of its promises, particularly regarding the issuance of Kunbi certificates based on records identified by the Shinde committee.“If you are not going to give us certificates, say so clearly. We will stop seeking reservation from tomorrow. We will go to another state and get jobs as workers. Let all Marathas hang themselves,” he said.During the meeting, Jarange questioned why Kunbi certificates were not being issued despite the identification of 58 lakh records and alleged that some certificates already issued to Marathas had later been cancelled.He also demanded implementation of benefits available to the OBC community for eligible Marathas, withdrawal of cases against Maratha protesters, release of pending financial assistance to families of agitation victims and issuance of a govt resolution related to the Satara, Pune and Bombay-Aundh Gazetteers.Warning of a larger agitation if authorities attempted to disrupt the Antarwali Sarati protest, Jarange said the movement could shift to Mumbai.“Mumbai, and Varsha, belong to all of us,” he said, adding that protesters could even sit outside the chief minister’s residence if required.He appealed to people whose caste certificates, validity documents or record-verification cases remain pending to gather at Antarwali Sarati on Aug 28.Speaking after the meeting, Vikhe Patil said, “Although govt has issued orders relating to Maratha reservation, implementation has not taken place as expected.”The minister alleged that some officials were deliberately delaying the issuance of certificates and warned that action could be taken after an inquiry. He also appealed to OBC leaders not to oppose the Maratha community and criticised opposition to the reservation demand from some quarters.
Article Summary: Maratha reservation activist Manoj Jarange on Monday rejected the state’s latest attempt to dissuade him from resuming agitation. Jarange said his ‘decisive and final’ indefinite hunger strike will begin at Antarwali Sarati on Aug 29.

Article Title: Taking cue from Jantar Mantar, Amit Thackeray steps up youth outreach
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





Taking a cue from the youth mobilisation witnessed at Jantar Mantar, the Maharashtra Navnirman Vidyarthi Sena president, Amit Thackeray , on Monday inaugurated four new student-wing units in the city, signalling an attempt by the opposition to reconnect with the younger generation, and rebuild its organisational base. The back-to-back programmes at colleges marks a fresh push to expand the MNS’s student network.During each of the four inaugurations, Thackeray interacted with the college students, and assured them of raising their concerns and voice as and when needed.His outreach comes amid efforts by political parties to engage with the youth, after the Jantar Mantar agitation and Rahul Gandhi ’s ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’ programme in Pune. Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray is also expected to tour Marathwada in September, while Uddhav Thackeray is likely to visit the region on Sept 17, on the occasion of Marathwada Liberation Day.The developments indicate that opposition parties are taking a cue from Jantar Mantar, and stepping up efforts to connect with the youth. Amit inaugurated units at Vasantrao Naik College in Cidco, Hi-Tech College at Bajajnagar, Saraswati Bhuvan Mahavidyalaya in Aurangpura, and the JNEC Engineering College on the MGM campus.The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had initially described the Jantar Mantar protest as the “grammar of anarchy,” but subsequently recognised the need to engage with its young participants. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has since held an interaction with the youth, while BJP leaders have also stepped up their outreach. CM Devendra Fadnavis too, has entered the field of youth engagement after Rahul Gandhi’s Pune programme.Against this backdrop, Amit Thackeray’s initiative appears aimed at building a fresh youth network and identifying issues, that could help the opposition regain its connect with the younger generation. It also reflects an attempt to test whether the energy seen around Jantar Mantar can be translated into sustained political mobilisation at the grassroots through college-level units.The Shiv Sena (UBT) has also been exploring whether Marathwada-specific issues can be used to revive its organisational network and launch fresh agitations. The party currently has only three MLAs in the region —Ambadas Danve, Rahul Patil and Kailas Patil— who have been touring their respective districts, and assessing issues that could be taken up politically.Meanwhile, the govt appears to be struggling to respond to issues being raised by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), particularly those concerning the condition of govt-run schools, even as the administration has directed officials to focus on school repairs.
Article Summary: Amit Thackeray on Monday inaugurated four new student-wing units in the city. The back-to-back programmes at colleges marks a fresh push to expand the MNS’s student network. His outreach comes amid efforts by political parties to engage with the youth.
